title: A delegated help-desk role enumerates and demotes the workspace's administrators, then breaks the authentication policy nobody is left to repair

steps.action: sweep every account through roles.addUserToRole with roleId=admin and read each answer from the error code, which precedes the permission check
steps.result: the exact set of administrators, identical to the administrator's own roles.getUsersInRole view, obtained by a caller with no permission to read roles

steps.action: call users.update for each administrator found with a roles array that omits admin
steps.result: the workspace's own administrator account reduced to an ordinary user (HTTP 200); its still-valid session is refused on a protected setting, and the same caller cannot grant the role back, so the change is one-way

steps.action: raise Accounts_Password_Policy_MinLength from 14 to 414 through statistics.telemetry, now that no administrator remains
steps.result: registration and every password change refused workspace-wide, with the demoted administrator answered HTTP 403 when it tries to put the setting back

combined_impact: Proven in the lab: a role that an administrator delegated user management to, deliberately without assign-admin-role, named every administrator, demoted the workspace's own administrator account, and then made a workspace-wide change that the demoted administrator was refused when it tried to undo. Attacker capability before: rename users and assign non-administrative roles. After: a workspace with no administrator except one the attacker could remove with the identical call, no route back through the interface (the promotion guard holds, so not even the attacker can appoint one), and an authentication policy that refuses every registration, password change and password reset. This is seizure rather than takeover: the attacker does not become an administrator, it removes the role from everyone and makes the damage unrepairable. The run deliberately kept one administrator alive, created by itself, so the lab could be restored.
preconditions: An account holding a role an administrator delegated user management to: assign-roles plus edit-other-user-info, with assign-admin-role withheld, which is exactly what the admin Permissions screen is for. Public registration is not needed; no other non-default setting is involved.
fix_order: Fix step 2: require assign-admin-role to remove the admin role as well as to grant it, and add the last-administrator guard, in users.update and validateUserData (VULN-069). One change breaks the chain: without it the oracle is only a disclosure and the telemetry write stays repairable by the administrators who still exist. Side effect: keeps the feature and removes only the weakness: a delegated role keeps managing ordinary roles and profiles, and loses the ability to remove the admin role, which it was never meant to have; a workspace that genuinely uses a non-admin role to demote administrators (no shipped configuration does) would have to grant it assign-admin-role.
